subject: OCCURS clause
notes: Rule (cite.py OK §13.18.38.4 15)): 'Data-name-3 defines a numeric data item that contains the current capacity of the associated table. Data-name-3 shall not be referenced as a receiving operand.' (the second sentence restates §13.18.38.3 SR32, cite.py OK, which excepts the variable-table format SET). Half 1: the register is a read-only view over CobolDynTable.Capacity (= _count, the current capacity §8.5.1.9.1). Probes (out13/probe/occurs-p2): gr1.cob DCAP=3 after three receiving refs; gr14b.cob RCAP 2 -> 4 -> 5 through implicit growth; gr15.cob SET RCAP TO 3 / SET RCAP TO X (X=4) / SET RCAP UP BY 2 read back 3/4/2; MOVE RCAP TO X is legal (sending). Half 2: every receiving position tried is refused COBOL1523 ('the CAPACITY register … shall not be a receiving operand except in a SET statement Format 14 (ISO §13.18.38.3 SR30–32)'): MOVE, MOVE to two receivers, ADD, SUBTRACT, COMPUTE, INITIALIZE, ACCEPT, STRING INTO, INSPECT REPLACING, PERFORM VARYING, CALL BY REFERENCE; CALL … BY CONTENT RCAP is accepted (not a receiving reference). Both halves verified. Read half is witnessed by conformance:cases/_unassigned/dyn_capacity_read and conformance:cases/8.5.1.9-Dynamic-capacity-tables/dyn_implicit_grow, but no spec-derived test pins the receiving-operand refusal (no .err or unit test names COBOL1523), so test-ref left empty = test-needed (one negative golden per receiving verb family). || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2014, 2023 (Format 4 only)
